official_source.reference: Kroes et al. (2017), SWAP version 4: Theory description and user manual, Wageningen Environmental Research Report 2780
official_source.documented_scheme: implicit, backward, finite difference scheme with explicit linearization of hydraulic conductivities
official_source.documented_legacy_time_step_rule: increase, keep or halve the timestep from the number of nonlinear iterations needed for convergence
official_source.documented_head_criteria: CritDevH1CP and CritDevH2CP constrain relative and absolute pressure-head changes between nonlinear iterations, not full-step versus two-half temporal discrepancy

source_bound_interpretation.reason: The documented CritDevH criteria are nonlinear iteration convergence criteria. Reusing their numerical values as a SWAP5 temporal acceptance tolerance would silently change their meaning and is not source justified.
source_bound_interpretation.reason_2: Legacy timestep adaptation is iteration-count based and does not estimate temporal truncation error. SWAP5 transaction acceptance intentionally requires an explicit model-owned temporal signal instead.

relation_to_fsi20_measurements.measured_fixed_horizon_behavior: pressure-head endpoint differences decrease monotonically under refinement and the fine apparent order approaches approximately one on the exact prescribed-head fixture
relation_to_fsi20_measurements.qualification_limit: Do not use a Richardson multiplier solely from the method label. The measured full-versus-two-half discrepancy is not a fixed multiplier of fine-reference endpoint error across all retry horizons, so any quantitative error-bound interpretation requires separate qualification.

candidate_semantic_consequence.meaning_that_can_be_defended_now: direct full-step versus two-half pressure-head endpoint discrepancy
candidate_semantic_consequence.meaning_not_yet_defended: universal estimate or upper bound of the two-half candidate's error to the exact Richards solution
